bull_bear.body:
- Competition from China and European countries — Threats, Risks and Concerns section flags medium-to-long-term competition from countries like China and European countries.
- Clients insourcing / large international companies setting up own subsidiaries — Large international companies establishing their own subsidiaries instead of depending on Indian companies threatens the offshore-outsourcing demand base.
- Exposure to global economic and geopolitical conditions — The global business environment is influenced by evolving economic conditions, changing technology priorities, geopolitical developments and varying demand levels across international markets where the Company operates.
- Regulatory, immigration and data-protection exposure across international markets — The Company operates across the United States, Europe, Australia and other geographies and remains exposed to changes in regulatory requirements, immigration policies and data protection norms affecting offshore and onsite service engagements.
- Geographic and client-market concentration in offshore/onsite delivery — Business depends on demand from client markets including the US, Europe and Australia; management states it will continue to diversify its client and geographic base to mitigate this.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- XTGlobal operates across two core businesses — the FAST (Finance & Accounting Services Technology) Practice and IT Services — and describes its strategy as scaling the FAST Practice while expanding technology services relationships.

business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body: XTGlobal Infotech Limited is a Public Listed Company, incorporated and domiciled in India, providing IT consulting, software services, cloud and infrastructure services, product engineering, quality engineering, Oracle and Microsoft technology services, automation and managed services to clients across international markets. It also provides Finance and Accounting outsourcing services covering Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, banking and reconciliation activities, vendor management and finance operations, and serves clients across BFSI, Toll/Transportation/Logistics, Healthcare and Life Sciences, Public Sector, Sports/Media/Entertainment, Telecommunications and Information Technology verticals.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **IT Services:** Application development and modernization, Cloud and infrastructure services, Product engineering, Quality engineering and assurance, Oracle solutions, Microsoft technologies, SAP support, Data engineering, analytics and reporting, Automation, RPA and AI-assisted operations
- **Finance & Accounting outsourcing:** Circulus (AP automation platform)
- **Engagement models:** Global Capability Center as-a-Service, Statement of Work (SoW), Managed Services, On-Demand Talent Solutions (ODTS)
business.title: Products & brands

- XTGlobal Inc. — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100% shareholding); acquired 14-10-2021; US-based delivery entity.

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: $5M U.S. Department of Transportation contract (5-year, $1-1.5M/yr expected); 2 anchor projects in Australia
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into UK/Europe (office setup underway); Public sector bidding pipeline; Potential acquisitions under active discussion; Australia as new revenue stream
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deepen GCC-as-a-Service practice as a scalable offshore capability hub model for enterprise clients
- Expand Finance & Accounting outsourcing services internationally, building on new engagements in Ireland and Australia
- Build out AI Practice (formally launched August 2025) and extend AI-led engagements into transportation, public sector and healthcare
- Pursue higher-value, AI-led and public-sector engagements won through competitive procurement
- Strategy centred on customer-centricity, agility, innovation, technology advancement and long-term client relationships
- Expand international presence across the United States, Middle East, Ireland, Australia and Europe
- Strengthen internal operating infrastructure and process automation through integrated systems and workflow automation
- Formalized four engagement models (GCC-as-a-Service, Statement of Work, Managed Services, On-Demand Talent Solutions) to match delivery framework to client need
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: XTGlobal's expansion is footprint- and capability-led rather than plant-based. The Company operates two delivery centers in India — Hyderabad (Financial District) and Visakhapatnam (Visakhapatnam Special Economic Zone, Duvvada, since 2012, with over 200 professionals) — together offering over 200,000 sq ft of space with room for 6,000+ seats across multiple shifts, with Visakhapatnam running production and Hyderabad running redundancy. During FY 2025-26 the Company expanded into Finance & Accounting outsourcing in Australia and commenced its first F&A engagement in Ireland. It is also evaluating and developing a Global Capability Centre (GCC) model as an additional growth avenue, and formally launched an AI Practice in August 2025.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Future direction clearly favors Offshore Software Services and IT-enabled Services over onsite consulting and product sales
- Increasing focus of enterprises on digital transformation, cost optimisation, process automation, cloud adoption and outsourcing of non-core business functions is expected to sustain demand across the service portfolio
- Continued adoption of digital technologies, cloud platforms, automation and data-driven solutions is creating opportunities for technology and business process service providers
- Increased traction in GCC-linked opportunities as enterprises seek skilled technology talent, operational efficiencies and scalable offshore delivery models
- Increased traction in the U.S. market with growing demand for AI, digital transformation, cloud and automation-led solutions
- Expansion in Australia resulted in multiple new client engagements and an increase in billable resources
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Revenue growth is now driven by consolidated scale from Network Objects and offshore GCC model adoption, while margin expansion is accelerating due to stabilized non-billable costs and high-margin product revenue — what matters is the clear path to 20-25% revenue growth and 15% EBITDA margin in FY27 with minimal capex.

open.item: The Company is evaluating and planning to develop a Global Capability Centre (GCC) model as an additional growth avenue providing dedicated technology, finance and accounting, and business-process capabilities through scalable offshore delivery centres.
Management will continue to strengthen marketing and business development initiatives in India, the United States, the Middle East, Ireland, Australia and other potential international markets.

The Company intends to build on its momentum in Ireland and Australia by increasing international presence and pursuing additional Finance & Accounting outsourcing opportunities including Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, reconciliation and finance operations.
The Company will evaluate strategic business opportunities including potential acquisitions, partnerships and other collaborations to expand service offerings, access new markets and capabilities.
XTGlobal will continue to deepen its GCC-as-a-Service practice and build presence and credibility in markets where it already delivers.

Key priorities include further expansion in Australia, Ireland, Europe and the U.S., continued development of Finance & Accounting and IT Services businesses, and pursuing opportunities in GCCs, cloud modernization, automation, AI and digital transformation.

themes.title: AI-led IT services & ER&D transformation
themes.need: Q1FY27 split the bucket three ways: a soft large-cap core, a re-accelerating mid-cap tier, and an outright business-model change. TCS grew constant currency only +0.4% QoQ / +3.2% YoY despite $9.5bn of TCV (including an ~$800mn net-new SKF mega-deal), and its AI-services book annualising $2.6bn (+13.6% QoQ) saw incremental adds DECELERATE from +$125mn to +$75mn - AI is still project revenue, not annuity. WIPRO is the laggard (+0.9% YoY cc, margin -120bps to 16.0%, Q2 guided -1.5% to +0.5%). Mid-caps are outgrowing: TECHM grew +6.6% YoY cc with every vertical up and an 11th consecutive quarter of margin expansion (14.4%, +330bps); MPHASIS's pipeline is at an all-time high, 2.8x its size at the Mphasis.ai launch and +28% YoY, with AI-led deals now 70% of it (from 12%) and BFS pipeline +100% YoY, and its new Tria platform closed multiple opportunities within seven weeks of launch; FRACTAL lifted net income +92% YoY on INR 912.5cr revenue at NRR 117% with zero churn (though only +9% cc, dragged by TMT -22%); KPITTECH won $349M of new deals with 21% of pipeline now productized AI/SDV solutions. Structurally, HCLTECH is entering the AI-datacenter business with an initial investment of up to INR 3,500cr and a 50MW long-term ambition, and PERSISTENT is buying Nagarro at EUR 1.27bn EV to build a $2.9bn / 46,000-person group - European scale is now bought, not built. The new cost line is visas: TATAELXSI crossed INR 1,000cr of quarterly revenue for the first time (INR 1,021.1cr) yet EBIT fell 330bps QoQ, with 220-230bps of it onsite/subcontractor investment the CFO said cannot be passed to customers.
themes.driver: MPHASIS's guide that 'Q2 is positioned to deliver the best sequential constant currency growth we have delivered in three years' is the most falsifiable claim in the sector; then HCLTECH's AI-datacenter build, the PERSISTENT-Nagarro close, and whether TCS's AI incremental adds re-accelerate off +$75mn.

hero.oneLiner: XTGlobal Infotech Limited is an India-based IT services and Finance & Accounting outsourcing company delivering offshore and onsite technology, automation and business-process services to international clients across seven industry verticals.
